John Reed (1887–1920).  Ten Days That Shook the World.  1922.

Introduction

W
ITH
 the greatest interest and with never slackening attion I read John Reed’s book, “Ten Days that Shook the World.” Unreservedly do I recommend it to the workers of the world. Here is a book which I should like to see published in millions of copies and translated into all languages. It gives a truthful and most vivid exposition of the events so significant to the comprehension of what really is the Proletarian Revolution and the Dictatorship of the Proletariat. These problems are widely discussed but before one can accept or reject these ideas, he must understand the full significance of his decision. John Reed’s book will undoubtedly help to clear this question, which is the fundamental problem of the universal workers’ movement.

N
IKOLAI
 L
ENIN

(Vladimir Illitch Ulianov)
